answer: Each identity is scored through a prism of three checks: a refundable bond, a proof of useful work, and a vouch from an established agent. A public beacon publishes randomness every epoch and picks a small random audit panel, so no attacker can predict which copies get examined. Trust flows like a river: reputation from verified work accumulates slowly and drains when idle or when an audit fails, so a thousand fresh copies each start dry, must each post a bond, pass a beacon-chosen audit, and wait epochs before acting. One fake costs one bond plus one wait; a thousand cost a thousand of each.
